{
  "candidate_rtl": "module pw_alu #(
    parameter WIDTH = 64
)(
    input wire [WIDTH-1:0] a, b,
    input wire [2:0] Oper,
    output reg [WIDTH-1:0] sum
);
    localparam LEVELS = $clog2(WIDTH);

    wire [WIDTH-1:0] axb;
    wire [WIDTH-1:0] add_a, add_b;
    wire [WIDTH-1:0] bit_p;
    wire [WIDTH-1:0] pg [0:LEVELS];
    wire [WIDTH-1:0] gg [0:LEVELS];
    wire [WIDTH-1:0] carry;
    wire [WIDTH-1:0] arithmetic_result;
    wire cin;
    wire inversion_parity;
    wire arithmetic_enable;
    wire or_enable, and_enable, xor_enable;
    wire [WIDTH-1:0] xor_result;

    assign axb = a ^ b;
    assign add_a = a ^ {WIDTH{Oper[1]}};
    assign add_b = b ^ {WIDTH{Oper[0]}};
    assign inversion_parity = Oper[1] ^ Oper[0];
    assign bit_p = axb ^ {WIDTH{inversion_parity}};
    assign cin = Oper[1] | Oper[0];

    assign pg[0] = bit_p;
    assign gg[0][0] = (add_a[0] & add_b[0]) | (bit_p[0] & cin);

    genvar i, s;
    generate
        for (i = 1; i < WIDTH; i = i + 1) begin : initial_generate
            assign gg[0][i] = add_a[i] & add_b[i];
        end
        for (s = 0; s < LEVELS; s = s + 1) begin : prefix_stage
            for (i = 0; i < WIDTH; i = i + 1) begin : prefix_bit
                if (i >= (1 << s)) begin : combine
                    assign gg[s+1][i] = gg[s][i] |
                        (pg[s][i] & gg[s][i-(1 << s)]);
                    assign pg[s+1][i] = pg[s][i] & pg[s][i-(1 << s)];
                end else begin : pass_through
                    assign gg[s+1][i] = gg[s][i];
                    assign pg[s+1][i] = pg[s][i];
                end
            end
        end
        for (i = 0; i < WIDTH; i = i + 1) begin : result_bit
            if (i == 0) begin : first_bit
                assign carry[i] = cin;
            end else begin : remaining_bits
                assign carry[i] = gg[LEVELS][i-1];
            end
        end
    endgenerate

    assign arithmetic_result = bit_p ^ carry;
    assign arithmetic_enable = ~Oper[2] & ~(Oper[1] & Oper[0]);
    assign or_enable = (Oper == 3'b011);
    assign and_enable = (Oper == 3'b100);
    assign xor_enable = (Oper == 3'b101) | (Oper == 3'b110);
    assign xor_result = axb ^ {WIDTH{Oper[1]}};

    always @* begin
        sum = (arithmetic_result & {WIDTH{arithmetic_enable}})
            | ((a | b) & {WIDTH{or_enable}})
            | ((a & b) & {WIDTH{and_enable}})
            | (xor_result & {WIDTH{xor_enable}});
    end
endmodule",
  "bottleneck": "The likely arithmetic bottleneck is carry propagation through the inferred addition/subtraction datapaths, followed by operation selection. The original RTL also describes three separately selectable arithmetic expressions.",
  "rewrite": "Use one shared add/subtract datapath with a parallel-prefix carry network. Operation 000 computes a+b, 001 computes a+~b+1, and 010 computes ~a+b+1. Fold carry-in into the least-significant generate term. For WIDTH=32, carry generation uses five prefix stages. Combine arithmetic and logical results with decoded masks rather than a priority selection chain.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "The explicit logarithmic carry network is intended to reduce maximum arithmetic data arrival relative to a ripple-like mapping. The actual gain depends on SKY130HD mapping, buffering, and interface loading; no STA result or numerical improvement is claimed.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Prefix carry generation adds intermediate propagate/generate gates and routing, while sharing the arithmetic datapath avoids three independent adders. High-fanout operation controls may require buffering. Compliance with the 6534.767360um2 area cap and electrical constraints requires evaluation with the specified flow.",
  "functional_boundaries": "Preserves the module name, parameter, port widths, unsigned ports, combinational behavior, WIDTH-bit truncation, all seven operations, and zero output for Oper=111. Supports positive WIDTH values, including WIDTH=1 and non-power-of-two widths. Internal arithmetic values for logical operations are masked from the output. No state, latency, latches, memories, assumptions, assertions, or undefined outputs are introduced. Equivalence and physical checks remain to be run."
}
